## What it is

Every number in an owner-run business usually goes through the owner: sales in the accounting tool, jobs in a spreadsheet, updates on WhatsApp, the rest in people's heads. I fix the numbers first, then build the screen on top. I pull your numbers out of every system, then check every total against your own books before you see the screen.

- **Your screen**: Money in, money out and what's owed; every job with its owner and due date; who on the team is producing; answers to plain questions from your own data; numbers that stay put when someone leaves.
- **One build**: A delivery business doing about 80 jobs a day with 6 drivers kept its jobs in spreadsheets and its drivers on a separate app, and paid someone to type up the day at 6pm. I built them one system instead: the office books a job, the driver closes it with photos of the signed invoice, and each customer sees their own orders as they move. The code and the data are theirs at handover.
- **What comes after**: Once your numbers are connected and checked, I can build a custom app on top of them. Automations only work once the workflow underneath is connected, so that part always comes first.

Four steps, about four weeks: a 30-minute call → one scoping call (I write down what "done" means in one sentence, then I quote) → your numbers, cleaned and checked, on your own accounts → your screen goes live, with recorded walkthroughs for your team.

## How it works: the six layers

Agentic workspaces. I build the six layers that let AI agents work beside your staff — on your data, on your say-so. Your people set the rules, the agents do the legwork, and every hand-off is on the record.

- **01 Context** — You and your team write down who you are, what you sell and why, who owns what, and how you sound. The agents read it before they touch anything.
- **02 Operational data** — Shared notes, not a guess. People add to it, agents keep it tidy, and everyone looks it up before they act.
- **03 AI agents** — One team, two kinds of member: every agent has one job and a person it answers to. A director agent keeps them in step.
- **04 The workspace** — One shared workspace — a folder for every client and job — where people and agents pick up each other's work, and every change is kept.
- **05 Ledger** — Who did what, and when: the agent that drafted it, the person who checked it. You can read it, question it and undo it.
- **06 Admin panel** — One view of how the week is going, and the few decisions only you should make. Nothing goes out in your name that you did not allow.

I start with the foundation — your context and data — built on your real records in about four weeks. The agents, the workspace, the ledger and your panel follow. You own all of it.

About four weeks from scoping call to a working agentic workspace. Call → Scoping call (scope + quote, you approve) → Build (on your accounts, your real data) → Handover (recordings + SOPs) → Monthly (optional, cancel anytime).

I build until what's in the scope works. Not a refund. The result. If what's in the signed scope isn't working on the day I said it would be, I keep building until it does, at no extra cost. Anything outside the scope is a new scope.

You own all of it:

- **Where your data lives** — In your own workspaces, drives and databases, named tool by tool in the scope.
- **Whose accounts and keys** — Yours. I get scoped access to build and hand it back at handover.
- **Who changes things** — You, after handover. You never need me to use it.
- **Getting it out** — Everything exports as files. No format only I can open.

No PSG or EDG paperwork. Grant approval takes four to six months; the build takes about four weeks.
